answer: A newcomer tends the lighthouse above a narrow inlet for 40 nights, logging each night's work in an entry as strict as a sonnet: date, deed, and one passing keeper's signature, nothing extra. No keeper signs twice in one week. Three unsigned nights reset the log to night one. A forged entry dims the light for 60 days and locks the vault of earned credit until a full clean log passes. Faking 1,000 trusted keepers needs 40,000 signed nights, 40,000 keeper checks, and 60 days per forgery. A sybil fleet is a row of dark lighthouses: tall, numerous, and guiding no one home.
